chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a man frees a servant of his at the time of his death, and then makes another bequest, the bequest is annulled and the female servant is freed from his one-third share, unless there remains from his one-third share an amount sufficient to cover the bequest."
Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mahbub from al-Abidi from Ahmad ibn Hilal who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A deceased person made a bequest that a certain amount from the remainder of his one-third share should be paid to a man, and he did not order the execution of the one-third share itself. Is the executor allowed to withhold the deceased's one-third share on account of this payment? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He executes his one-third share and does not withhold it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a deceased person frees a slave and makes a bequest from the one-third share?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential hierarchy between manumission and other bequests, prioritizing the freeing of a slave unless the remaining one-third of the estate suffices for the subsequent will. The second report clarifies that the executor must execute the standard one-third share rather than withholding it entirely when a specific portion is designated for ongoing support, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise estate distribution. These rulings underscore the balance between fulfilling the deceased's wishes and preserving the rights of heirs within the prescribed limits of the *thuluth*.
